findings: selectedMarkPerm extends the actual selectedVisitTwinPerm to the complete Mark P sum, with identity on every original vertex. Its involution follows constructorwise from the actual twin involution. It accepts actual finite crossing supports and no externally supplied pairing or mark permutation.

selectedMarkPerm_evaluation uses G1 and actual visit-position evaluation to show that switching preserves the planar endpoint. Both visits retain the same crossing identity and hence the same crossingPoint. This does not identify their distinct traversal nodes or quotient them by equality of planar points.

The composition order is exactly the source rule. Equiv.trans first applies selectedMarkPerm and then markSuccessor, so smoothingSuccessor(a)=rho(selectedMarkPerm(a)). At a selected visit this equals rho(twin(a)); at each vertex and unselected visit it equals rho(a). It is not the different operation of taking rho(a) and then switching that output node.

Consequently the selected node keeps its original identity, corresponding to its incoming arc, while it leaves by the twin's old outgoing slot. owner is the orbit class of that original node, implementing the source incoming-visit endpoint convention. The finite-node rule and endpoint-evaluation equality are proved here; a full correspondence to regular planar carrier curves remains a later geometric theorem.

selectedMarkPerm_commute derives commuting actual slot switches constructorwise from crossing-fiber membership. selectedMarkPerm_union_of_disjoint requires actual support disjointness, and its Equiv.trans order gives theta(S union T)=theta(S) after theta(T). No incorrect union rule for overlapping supports is asserted.

smoothingSuccessor_union_of_disjoint correspondingly gives rho(S union T)=rho(S) after theta(T). Thus adding disjoint switches acts on outgoing slots of the already constructed successor. This supplies the concrete finite commutation/extension algebra without asserting that arbitrary supports only split cycles.

Component is literally Quotient of the canonical SameCycle setoid of the constructed smoothingSuccessor. SameCycle means existence of an integer power of this permutation. No carrier partition or orbit correspondence is supplied as a hypothesis, and equal planar crossing points do not determine component equality.

owner_eq_iff identifies equality of the quotient classes exactly with actual successor orbit membership. owner_successor and owner_predecessor use one-step orbit invariance; owner_surjective follows quotient induction, so every component has an actual mark representative.

componentFintype follows from the finite actual mark domain. component_card_pos exhibits the owner of original vertex0; it is valid even when Crossing P and S are empty. This retains the source crossing-free polygon case instead of constructing components from a potentially empty visit-only list.

smoothingSuccessor_empty equals the actual original markSuccessor. component_empty_subsingleton is then derived by representing two arbitrary quotient elements by actual marks and invoking the proved all-marks SameCycle theorem. Together with a vertex-owner inhabitant, component_card_empty proves exactly one component for empty support.

No independent-support hypothesis is hidden or needed for these definitions and permutation/orbit identities. The stronger source conclusions that selected twins lie on distinct final carriers, every selected operation splits, the count is |S|+1, inherited cyclic order is preserved and all visits have noncrossing ownership are not claimed by this packet.
